title: Korea EDCF — Tanzania AI and digital technology training institute, 2026
description:
The ministry's own sentences, in the Korean it published in:

> 재정경제부는 제159차 대외경제협력기금(EDCF) 운용위원회(위원장: 재정경제부 장관)를 서면 개최하고, 탄자니아 AI‧디지털 기술교육기관 건립 사업 승인안과 EDCF 운용관리규정 개정안 등을 의결하였다.

> 탄자니아 AI‧디지털 기술교육기관 건립 사업은 탄자니아의 AI·디지털 산업 인력 양성을 위해 AI, 로보틱스, 데이터분석, IoT 등 4개 학과를 운영하는 첨단 기술교육기관을 건립하는 사업으로, 1.7억불 규모의 EDCF 차관이 지원될 예정이다.

> 동 사업은 교육시설과 캠퍼스 건축, AI Lab‧IoT‧로보틱스‧드론‧3D 프린터 등 AI 교육·실습 기자재 구축, ICT 및 네트워크 시스템 구축 및 교육과정 개발과 운영(O&M) 지원 등으로 구성된다.

> 동 사업은 우리 기업만 수주할 수 있는 ‘구속성(tied)’ 차관 사업으로, 금번 EDCF 차관 지원을 통해 AI, 에듀테크, 건설 등과 관련된 우리 기업의 아프리카 시장 진출 기회가 마련될 것으로 기대된다.

Scope, from those sentences and stated here in English as CC's reading rather than the ministry's words: an advanced technical training institute running four departments — AI, robotics, data analytics and IoT — comprising teaching facilities and campus construction, AI teaching and practical equipment (AI Lab, IoT, robotics, drones, 3D printers), a high-performance AI training facility built around AI compute, HBM and high-speed networking, ICT and network systems, curriculum development, and operations and maintenance support. The loan is tied: only Korean firms may win the contracts.
original_amount: US$170,000,000 — stated by the ministry as 1.7억불, a figure it gives in dollars itself

title: Mars Growth Capital (Liquidity/MUFG) — NALA payment-rails credit facility, 2026

NALA said the facility will support "reliable and scalable payment infrastructure across international remittance corridors," including stablecoin-linked payment corridors.

title: Vodacom Tanzania M-Pesa Platform Modernisation \u2014 Fintech 2.0
description: Vodacom Tanzania PLC completed a $28 million investment to migrate its M-Pesa platform from the legacy G2 system to a next-generation 'Fintech 2.0' platform, announced April 2026. The 15-month project, completed April 2026, modernises Tanzania's leading mobile money platform (30 million customers, ~41% market share, 600,000+ merchants). Key improvements: 1,000+ transactions/second capacity; system updates without service interruption (previously required nightly downtime); enhanced security; faster product deployment. The upgrade is part of a wider $100M modernisation programme announced Sep 2025 (Vodacom Tanzania 25th anniversary). The new platform also supports Tanzania becoming the first African country to enable M-Pesa contactless (tap-to-pay) payments.

The expanded network is intended to support government services, education, healthcare and business development across the two islands.

title: Dada Wakili — a digital legal assistant enabling access to justice for women in Tanzania
description: project Title: DADA WAKILI: A DIGITAL LEGAL ASSISTANT ENABLING ACCESS TO JUSTICE FOR WOMEN IN TANZANIA AND BEYOND. This project aims to promote the rule of law and drive inclusive economic growth by scaling Dada Wakili to provide timely and reliable legal information to women and frontline legal advisors. This supports economic empowerment and social well-being by removing legal barriers that prevent women from accessing and owning property and land, asserting inheritance rights, seeking protection from violence, resolving family disputes and participating fully in trade and enterprise.

Helios Towers is Africa's leading independent telecoms infrastructure company, operating towers on over 14,000 sites and serving 144+ million mobile subscribers across Africa. The investment directly enables mobile internet and data services for underserved rural populations.

title: Axian-Rostam Consortium Acquisition of Tigo Tanzania and Zantel from Millicom
description: On 7 April 2022, a consortium led by Axian Telecom (together with Rostam Azizi) completed the acquisition of Millicom's entire Tanzanian telecom operations: MIC Tanzania Ltd (Tigo Tanzania) and Zanzibar Telecom (Zantel). The deal price was USD 100 million. The acquisition gave Axian strategic ownership in the EASSy cable landing station in Dar es Salaam, a consortium network of over 3,200 km backbone and 600 km metro fibre. The business was subsequently rebranded as Yas Tanzania. Axian announced a USD 500 million investment plan for Tanzanian network expansion over subsequent years.

title: ZTE grants $3.5 million USD for the Safe Zanzibar Project
description: In June 2015, ZTE corporation donated $3.5 million USD for the Safe Zanzibar Project which involves installing a CCTV surveillance system in Stone Town. The purpose of this project was to curb crime in Zanzibar, particularly in tourist areas.   According to the reporting from the Habarileo, the entire project was scheduled for completion by the end of 2015. Work plans included the installation of 300 full high definition cameras (FHD) on the main roads of the Stone Town and a command center in Malindi with a video wall and camera control center. The video surveillance system uses Geographic Information System (GIS), case library, and intelligent analysis tools. According to the engineer, with routine management, this system can facilitate sharing information among different administrative departments, utilizing security resources and improving efficiency  of controlling or responding rapidly to major accidents.
